title: Nobatia
capsule: Nobatia was a Christianized Nubian kingdom occupying Lower Nubia (the First to Third Cataracts region, spanning modern southernmost Egypt and northern Sudan), formed from earlier Meroitic populations following the collapse of Kush in the 4th century CE. Missionaries sent by Emperor Justinian I converted the Nobatian court to Chalcedonian Christianity around 543, though rival Monophysite missionaries also operated there; by the late 6th century Nobatia had merged with its southern neighbor Makuria to form a unified Nubian kingdom centered at Dongola. The combined state withstood two Arab attempts to conquer it (642, 652) and negotiated the Baqt treaty, one of history's longest-lived non-aggression pacts.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political existence of Nobatia is attested in Byzantine and early Arabic sources, but its precise northern and southern territorial boundaries at any given date are uncertain and debated among Nubian archaeologists.
